messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Help with Correlation Matrix
parts:
1. Well the code does not match that in the User Guide; for example, the "raw_data" variable should be the output of the "import_scn" function.
2. If I am correct, it seems you are only interested in the left hemisphere? Do you have the data for the right hemisphere, as well? The functions expect both "lh_*" and "rh_*" from the beginning. I can certainly update the code to allow for only 1 hemisphere's data, but currently that is not how it works. You can then later subset the data by keeping only the LH data.
3. Either way, the final error message is saying that the design matrix (created from "covars") does not match the data. That is, the number of rows in "covars" should match the rows in "lhrh". Please check that they are the same.

Please try to follow the code exactly and see if it works. If it doesn't work still, you can send me your data and I will try to figure out the code to avoid the error.
Chris

Hi Chris,


I managed to reach this section where I need to set the relevant graph-, vertex-, and edge-level attributes. 


g <- Map(function(x, y) llply(x, set_brainGraph_attr, atlas=atlas, modality=modality, group=y, .progress='text'), g, as.list(groups))

  could not find function "llply" 


Thanks,

Andi




On Tuesday, May 14, 2019 at 11:43:35 PM UTC+10, Chris Watson wrote:
1. Well the code does not match that in the User Guide; for example, the "raw_data" variable should be the output of the "import_scn" function.
2. If I am correct, it seems you are only interested in the left hemisphere? Do you have the data for the right hemisphere, as well? The functions expect both "lh_*" and "rh_*" from the beginning. I can certainly update the code to allow for only 1 hemisphere's data, but currently that is not how it works. You can then later subset the data by keeping only the LH data.
3. Either way, the final error message is saying that the design matrix (created from "covars") does not match the data. That is, the number of rows in "covars" should match the rows in "lhrh". Please check that they are the same.

Please try to follow the code exactly and see if it works. If it doesn't work still, you can send me your data and I will try to figure out the code to avoid the error.
Chris

On Mon, May 13, 2019 at 8:15 PM Dion <dses...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,  here are the command that I tried to use. Maybe I am mistakenly understand some of the syntax. Thanks


datadir <- paste0("~/Desktop/Project_3")
covars <- fread(paste0(datadir, '/covars.csv'), stringsAsFactors=TRUE)
lh_dk <- fread(paste0(datadir, '/lh_dk_thickness.csv'), stringsAsFactors=TRUE)

groups <- covars[, levels(Group)]

raw_data <- read.csv("lh_dk_thickness.csv")
lapply(seq_along(raw_data), function(x)
  assign(names(raw_data)[x], eval(raw_data[[x]]), envir=.GlobalEnv)

exclude.subs <- NULL)

lhrh <- lh_dk

densities <- seq(0.05, 0.20, 0.01)
N <- which(abs(densities - 0.10) < 0.001)

all.dat.resids <- get.resid(lhrh, covars=covars, exclude.cov='Group')


and I got error:

Error in fastLmPure(lmvars$X, y, method = 2) : 
  NROW(y) == nrow(X) is not TRUE

Your "g" object has 3 elements (i.e., 3 groups), each with 16 elements (graphs) which I assume are of different densities. All 48 of these graph objects should have the appropriate "Group" graph attribute. So,
g[[1]][[1]]$Group <- 'AD'
g[[1]][[2]]$Group <- 'AD'
...
g[[2]][[1]]$Group <- 'bvFTD'
...
g[[3]][[1]]$Group <- 'Control'
...

You can achieve this assignment simply using "for" loops.

Chris
